newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Shenzhen targets 15 pct growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China's Shenzhen targets 15 pct growth in 1997.

text.p: The southern boomtown of Shenzhen, China's first special economic zone, has set a target of 15 percent economic growth for this year, the Xinhua news agency said in an overnight report.
The city plans to achieve gross domestic product (GDP) of 112 billion yuan for 1997, it said quoting a municipal plan.
The target for GDP growth compared with growth of 16.4 percent in 1996 and national GDP growth of 9.7 percent last year.
The city plans to achieve a 16 percent increase in fixed-asset investment, a 3.3 percent increase of foreign trade, and a 16.9 percent increase of retail sales, it said.
The city plans to use $1.8 billion in foreign funds this year, down by 25 percent compared with last year, Xinhua quoted a local official as saying.
He warned last year's downward trend foreign fund inflows would have a negative impact on the local economy in 1997.
The city would try to attract more loans from foreign governments or international financial organisations, rather than making direct foreign investments its priority, he said.
The official gave no other details. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
